ORDER This order shall govern the disposal of these two miscellaneous criminal cases as they have arisen out of the same crime number of the same police station, hence, they are heard analogously and are being decided by this common order.
1. They are heard.
Perused the case-diary.

2. These are the first bail applications filed by applicants under Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 as they are implicated in connection with Crime No.232/2023 registered at Police Station Sendhwa Gramin, District Barwani (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366-A,
368, 376, 376 (2)(n), 34 of IPC, 1860 and Sections 3/4, 5/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

sentences.text: Counsel for the applicants has submitted that the applicants are innocent and have been falsely implicated in the present crime.

It is submitted that although the prosecutrix is said to be minor at the time of the incident, however, as per the statement of her father and mother, she is aged about more than 17 years and at the time of recording the evidence the Court has recorded her age as 17 years.
The prosecutrix is major and now she is residing with father of applicant Dinesh.
Prosecutrix is present in person to place her application for no objection in granting bail to the applicant- Dinesh in M.Cr.C. No.23918/2023.
Prosecutrix was called before the Court to confirm her age wherein admitted that she is 18 years old.

So far as applicants Jairam and Remalu are concerned,
they helped main accused Dinesh in taking the prosecutrix to his relative's house and thereafter they returned back.
The applicants are in custody since16.04.2023 and the final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Hence, it is submitted that the bail application be allowed and the applicants be released on bail.
5. Counsel for the respondent / State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer and prayed for rejection of the application.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the material available on record so also considering the quantity of contraband, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to extend benefit of bail to the applicants.
Hence, without commenting on the merits of the case, this bail application is allowed.

7. It is directed that applicants be released on bail on their furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each with one solvent surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for their appearance before the said Court on the dates given by the concerned Court during pendency of trial.

It is further directed that the applicants shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
8.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial, however, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the pre-condition of bail, it shall become ineffective.
9. These M.Cr.Cs stand allowed and disposed off.
Certified copy as per rules.
